text: # Open the Earnings Report, and a Trailer Starts: What Comes Next for Broadcom?
If hearing “earnings report” made your eyelids feel heavy, please don’t go to sleep yet.
This time, Broadcom didn’t just hand out a report card and say, “Okay, that’s it, we’re done.”
Turn the page, and a trailer for the next quarter begins—with numbers fit for leading roles.
First, the main feature: the results for this quarter.
Consolidated revenue was $29.591 billion.
Revenue from AI semiconductors was $16.7 billion.
The numbers are so huge that my mental calculator feels ready to quietly shut down.
You might want to say, “So basically, AI is doing great, right?”
But don’t fast-forward just yet.
The $16.7 billion is revenue from “AI semiconductors,” not revenue from the entire “semiconductor division.”
The whole company, the semiconductor division, and AI semiconductors: the labels sound similar, but each number covers a different range.
Take away the labels, and the whole discussion quickly gets lost.
Then the CEO steps in.
The CEO says demand for custom AI accelerators and networking remains very strong.
The CEO’s view of demand now joins the results.
Here, the story starts to move from “now” to “next.”
The big feature in the trailer is the forecast for consolidated revenue in the next quarter: “about $34.8 billion.”
Put next to this quarter’s $29.591 billion, it certainly catches the eye.
But the two figures have different roles.
The first is a forecast for the future; the second is a result that has already come in.
Even though both are revenue figures, they belong to different time frames.
So it’s too early to start celebrating in your head and say, “They’ve reached about $34.8 billion!”
A movie trailer may show exciting scenes, but that doesn’t guarantee how the full movie will unfold.
It’s fine to feel hopeful.
But don’t put a forecast in the seat for actual results.
The company also says that actual results may differ from its outlook, and that the difference may be important.
Don’t skip over this as a small note.
Keep it in mind along with the trailer.
One more thing to check before you leave.
The outlook for about $34.8 billion is also for the whole company’s revenue, not just a forecast for AI semiconductors.
If we take the talk of strong demand for AI and turn it straight into “all the figures are AI figures,” we end up starting a different movie.
The highlights this time are how three things connect: the results for AI semiconductors, the CEO’s view of demand, and the outlook for the whole company’s revenue next quarter.
An earnings report doesn’t have to end with judging the past.
You can also enjoy asking, “What happens next?”
But check the labels before you applaud.
When you can tell the main feature from the trailer, the numbers become more interesting.
## In one line
Broadcom reported $16.7 billion in AI-chip sales and forecast about $34.8 billion in total company revenue next quarter.
